        NVCleanstall Component Explanation

        The settings shown below reflect my preferred configuration for a clean, lightweight, minimal, and performance-focused NVIDIA driver installation.

        My general recommendation is to avoid NVIDIA App, GeForce Experience, overlays, telemetry, recording features, and other optional components unless you specifically need them. For most users, the classic NVIDIA Control Panel provides all the functionality required to manage the graphics card without adding unnecessary software, services, or background processes.

        Core Components

        Display Driver (Required)

        This is the core NVIDIA graphics driver responsible for graphics rendering, game performance, hardware acceleration, CUDA support, video decoding and encoding, and communication between Windows and your graphics card.

        Without this component, the GPU cannot operate properly and Windows will fall back to a basic display driver with significantly reduced functionality and performance.

        Recommendation: Always keep it. This is the only truly mandatory component and the foundation of the entire driver package.

        Legacy Control Panel

        Installs the classic NVIDIA Control Panel.

        This utility allows you to configure display settings, G-SYNC, V-SYNC, image scaling, color settings, monitor configuration, power management, low latency settings, and many other important driver options. Unlike NVIDIA App, the classic Control Panel is lightweight, mature, and focused entirely on driver configuration without additional overlays or consumer-oriented features.

        Recommendation: Keep it. For most users, it provides everything needed to manage the graphics card while remaining lightweight and efficient.

        Optional & specialized features

        HD Audio via HDMI

        Installs the NVIDIA High Definition Audio driver used to transmit audio through HDMI or DisplayPort connections. This component is only necessary if your monitor, television, soundbar, AV receiver, or other audio device receives sound directly from the graphics card through HDMI or DisplayPort.

        If you use motherboard audio, a dedicated sound card, USB audio devices, headphones connected to your PC, or an external DAC, this driver may not be necessary.

        Recommendation: Keep it only if you use audio through HDMI or DisplayPort. Otherwise, it can be safely removed.

        Microsoft Visual C++ 2017 Runtimes

        Installs Microsoft Visual C++ runtime libraries included with the NVIDIA driver package. Many modern systems already have newer versions of the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable installed through Windows updates, games, launchers, or other applications. Some NVIDIA components may rely on these libraries depending on the installed configuration.

        Recommendation: If your system already has up-to-date Visual C++ Redistributables installed, this package is usually redundant. If you are unsure, keeping it is perfectly safe and has virtually no impact on system performance.

        PhysX

        Installs NVIDIA PhysX runtime libraries. Although PhysX is no longer widely used in modern games, many older titles still depend on these libraries for compatibility or to enable advanced physics effects. Examples include Borderlands 2, Batman: Arkham Asylum, Batman: Arkham City, Mirror's Edge, Metro 2033, and several older Unreal Engine titles.

        Recommendation: Generally worth keeping because it requires very little disk space and may improve compatibility with older games. If you only play modern games and want the smallest possible installation, it can be removed.

        USB-C Driver

        Provides support for NVIDIA VirtualLink and USB-C functionality found on certain older graphics cards. This feature was primarily intended for VR headsets and devices connected through the USB-C port present on some RTX graphics cards.

        Recommendation: Remove it unless you specifically use a USB-C or VirtualLink connection on your graphics card.

        Telemetry & Background Services

        Telemetry

        Installs NVIDIA telemetry and diagnostic services. These services collect technical information, usage statistics, and diagnostic data related to NVIDIA software and hardware. While the performance impact is generally minimal, many users prefer not to install software components that provide no direct benefit to gaming or graphics performance.

        Recommendation: Remove it for a cleaner installation. It is not required for normal GPU operation.

        NV Platform Controllers & NVIDIA DLISR

        Installs support services used by certain NVIDIA software features and integrations, including image-processing and AI-enhanced technologies. Most users will never directly interact with this functionality.

        Recommendation: For a minimal installation, it can generally be removed unless you know a specific feature you use depends on it.

        FrameView SDK, Quadro View & Virtual Audio

        Features for performance monitoring, professional workstation environments, and virtual audio devices used by NVIDIA Broadcast/GameStream.

        Recommendation: Remove unless you specifically need workstation-oriented functionality, development frameworks, or actively use streaming and broadcasting features.

        NVIDIA App Components

        My personal preference is to avoid NVIDIA App whenever possible. While it offers useful features for some users, it also introduces additional services, overlays, update mechanisms, telemetry, and background processes that many people simply do not need.

        • NVIDIA App: Provides driver updates, game optimization, overlays, filters, screenshots, recording features.
        • NV Container: Background service used by various NVIDIA software components.
        • ShadowPlay: Provides Instant Replay, gameplay recording, screenshots, highlights, and streaming functionality.
        • NV Backend & MessageBus: Backend and communication services for NVIDIA App.

        Recommendation: Remove them unless you specifically require features such as gameplay recording, overlays, filters, automatic game optimization, NVIDIA Broadcast, screenshots, or streaming functionality.

        Recommended Minimal Configuration

        For the cleanest, lightest, and most streamlined NVIDIA driver installation, I generally recommend keeping only:

        • Display Driver
        • Legacy Control Panel
        • PhysX (optional, mainly for compatibility with older games)

        Everything else can be removed unless you have a specific need for it. This provides full functionality, low latency, and zero bloatware.

        Radeon Software Slimmer Components

        The settings shown below are based on a clean, minimal, and performance-focused AMD driver installation.

        These recommendations are primarily intended for a typical desktop gaming PC with a dedicated AMD graphics card. Some components may be required on specific systems, especially laptops, Ryzen APUs, systems with integrated cameras, Bluetooth audio devices, USB-C display output, advanced audio implementations, capture devices, or professional workloads.

        The goal is to remove unnecessary components while preserving normal graphics functionality and system stability. If you are unsure whether a component is needed on your system, it is generally safer to leave it installed.

        Components Options

        AMD ACP AFD HPD User Service

        Service related to AMD's Audio Co-Processor (ACP) platform that handles certain audio detection, device monitoring, and audio management functions used on supported hardware configurations.

        Recommendation: If you only use your PC for gaming and normal desktop use, it can usually be removed. Most desktop users will never require this service.

        AMD ACP BT Audio Filter Driver

        Bluetooth audio filter driver used by certain AMD Audio Co-Processor implementations. It assists with audio processing and communication for supported Bluetooth audio devices.

        Recommendation: Keep it only if you use Bluetooth audio devices that depend on AMD audio components. Otherwise it can usually be removed.

        AMD ACP BT LE Audio Device

        Provides support for Bluetooth Low Energy (LE Audio) functionality on supported devices.

        Recommendation: Remove it unless you specifically use LE Audio devices or hardware that depends on this functionality.

        AMD ACP BUS2

        Core bus driver for AMD Audio Co-Processor devices. It provides communication between the operating system and ACP-related audio hardware.

        Recommendation: Keep it if it is selected by default. Some systems rely on it for proper audio functionality. Desktop users without ACP-dependent audio may not need it.

        AMD ACP USB Audio Filter Driver

        Provides filtering and management functions for certain USB audio devices that interact with AMD audio subsystems.

        Recommendation: Most desktop users can usually remove it without affecting normal audio functionality.

        AMD Audio CoProcessor Bus Driver

        Driver used by AMD's Audio Co-Processor subsystem. It enables communication between the operating system and AMD ACP hardware components.

        Recommendation: Keep it if your system uses AMD ACP-related audio functionality. Removing it may break audio features on some systems, particularly laptops and certain Ryzen APU configurations.

        AMD Audio Filter Driver

        Provides additional audio processing, signal routing, and compatibility functions for certain AMD audio implementations. Depending on the hardware configuration, it may assist with microphone support, audio enhancements, or communication between audio-related drivers.

        Recommendation: Most desktop users can usually remove it without affecting normal operation. However, if you experience missing audio devices, microphone issues, or audio instability after removal, reinstalling it may be necessary.

        AMD Camera Capture Device

        Camera capture driver used primarily on laptops and systems equipped with integrated cameras. It allows supported camera hardware to communicate with Windows.

        Recommendation: Desktop users can remove it. Laptop users should keep it if they use the built-in webcam.

        AMD Display Driver

        This is the primary graphics driver responsible for GPU functionality, hardware acceleration, display output, 3D rendering, video acceleration, and gaming performance.

        Recommendation: Always keep it. This is the essential component required for the graphics card to function properly.

        AMD DVR64

        Component used by AMD Software for Radeon ReLive, Instant Replay, desktop recording, game capture, and certain streaming-related features. It operates alongside AMD's multimedia framework.

        Recommendation: Remove it if you never use AMD recording, Instant Replay, game capture, or streaming features. It is not required for normal gaming or graphics performance.

        AMD HDMI Audio Driver

        Provides audio transmission over HDMI and DisplayPort connections through the graphics card. This allows monitors, TVs, AV receivers, and other compatible devices to receive audio directly from the GPU.

        Recommendation: Keep it if your monitor, TV, receiver, or headset receives audio through HDMI or DisplayPort. Otherwise it can usually be removed.

        AMD High Definition Audio Controller

        Controller driver that enables HDMI and DisplayPort audio functionality provided by the graphics card.

        Recommendation: Keep it if you use audio through your GPU. Otherwise it can usually be removed along with the HDMI Audio Driver.

        AMD ISP Bridge Device

        Image Signal Processor component used mainly by integrated cameras and imaging hardware. It assists with communication between camera sensors and the operating system.

        Recommendation: Desktop users can remove it. Laptop users should keep it if they use the built-in webcam.

        AMD Kipudrv Device for MCDM

        Internal AMD driver component used by modern AMD driver architectures and Microsoft Compute Driver Model (MCDM) implementations.

        Recommendation: Leave it installed. Removing it is generally not recommended unless you fully understand the implications and have verified that your specific configuration does not require it.

        AMD Navi UCSI Driver

        Implements USB Type-C Connector System Software Interface (UCSI) support for compatible AMD graphics cards. It is primarily responsible for USB-C display functionality, DisplayPort Alternate Mode negotiation, and related USB-C communication features.

        Recommendation: Keep it if your graphics card includes a USB-C port or if you use USB-C display connectivity. Otherwise it can usually be removed without affecting standard graphics functionality.

        AMD Settings

        Installs the AMD Software: Adrenalin Edition user interface, including graphics settings, performance monitoring, tuning controls, Radeon Anti-Lag, Radeon Chill, display configuration, update management, recording features, and various gaming-related options.

        Recommendation: Keep it if you want access to AMD's software ecosystem and driver configuration tools. It can be removed if your goal is a driver-only installation and you do not need the Radeon control panel.

        AMD SoundWire Controller Driver

        Driver used by systems that support SoundWire audio devices. SoundWire is a modern digital audio interface commonly found in certain mobile and integrated hardware platforms.

        Recommendation: Most desktop users can remove it. Systems that rely on SoundWire audio hardware should keep it installed.

        AMD SoundWire Streaming Driver

        Streaming component associated with SoundWire audio devices and related audio transport functionality.

        Recommendation: Most users can remove it unless their hardware specifically relies on SoundWire technology.

        AMD Streaming Audio Filter Driver

        Used by AMD streaming, recording, and multimedia capture features to manage audio streams associated with those functions.

        Recommendation: Remove it if you do not use AMD streaming, recording, or capture functionality.

        AMD User Experience Program Installer

        Installs AMD's telemetry and user experience feedback program used to collect diagnostic and usage information.

        Recommendation: Remove it. Most users do not need telemetry services and removing it does not affect normal driver functionality.

        AMD WVR64

        AMD Wireless VR component used by certain wireless virtual reality solutions and VR streaming implementations.

        Recommendation: Remove it unless you specifically use wireless VR hardware or software that depends on it.

        Branding64

        Contains AMD branding resources, visual assets, logos, and cosmetic interface components used by AMD Software.

        Recommendation: Remove it if you want the most minimal installation possible. It is not required for graphics functionality.

        Camera IR Sensor GC1029

        Infrared camera sensor driver used by specific camera modules found mainly in laptops and mobile-oriented devices.

        Recommendation: Desktop users can remove it. Laptop users should keep it if their system uses this sensor.

        Camera RGB Sensor OV05C

        Camera sensor driver used by supported integrated camera hardware.

        Recommendation: Remove it unless your system specifically requires it.

        Camera RGB Sensor OV13B

        Camera sensor driver used by supported integrated camera hardware.

        Recommendation: Remove it unless your system specifically requires it.

        I2S Audio Driver

        Audio interface driver used by certain integrated audio implementations. I2S (Inter-IC Sound) is commonly used in laptops, embedded devices, and systems with integrated audio hardware.

        Recommendation: Desktop users can usually remove it. Laptop users and systems with integrated audio dependencies should keep it installed.

        IR Sensor HM1092

        Infrared sensor driver used by specific camera and facial recognition hardware.

        Recommendation: Remove it unless your device specifically uses this sensor.

        IR Sensor VD55G0

        Infrared sensor driver used by specific camera and imaging hardware configurations.

        Recommendation: Remove it unless your device specifically uses this sensor.

        Microsoft Visual C++ 2022 Redistributable (Existing)

        Checks for existing Microsoft Visual C++ runtime libraries required by AMD Software and many Windows applications.

        Recommendation: Keep it. Numerous applications and games depend on these runtime libraries.

        Microsoft Visual C++ 2022 Redistributable (Package)

        Installs the Microsoft Visual C++ runtime libraries included with the AMD driver package.

        Recommendation: Keep it unless you are absolutely certain that an equal or newer version is already installed on the system.

        RGB Sensor OV08X

        Camera sensor driver used by supported integrated webcam hardware.

        Recommendation: Desktop users can remove it. Laptop users should keep it if their webcam requires it.

        RyzenMasterSDK

        Software Development Kit that exposes hardware telemetry and control interfaces used by AMD Ryzen Master and certain third-party monitoring, benchmarking, tuning, and overclocking applications.

        Recommendation: If you do not use Ryzen Master or software that relies on its telemetry interfaces, it can usually be removed. For most gaming systems it is not required for normal CPU or GPU operation.

        Recommended Minimal Configuration

        For most desktop gaming systems with a dedicated AMD graphics card, I would keep only:

        • AMD Display Driver
        • AMD Settings (recommended if you want the Radeon software interface and driver controls)
        • AMD HDMI Audio Driver (only if you use HDMI or DisplayPort audio)
        • AMD High Definition Audio Controller (only if you use HDMI or DisplayPort audio)
        • AMD Navi UCSI Driver (only if your GPU supports and uses USB-C display output)
        • Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable

        Everything else can generally be removed if your goal is the cleanest and most lightweight AMD driver installation possible.

        Important: There is no single minimal configuration that is guaranteed to work on every AMD-based system. Laptops, Ryzen APUs, systems with integrated cameras, Bluetooth audio devices, advanced audio processing, USB-C display functionality, capture hardware, and certain OEM-specific configurations may require additional components. These recommendations are intended primarily for a standard desktop gaming PC with a dedicated AMD graphics card.

        Radeon Software Slimmer - Scheduled Tasks Explanation

        The scheduled tasks listed below are primarily associated with AMD Software Adrenalin, automatic updates, telemetry, installation maintenance, and auxiliary software features.

        The scheduled tasks listed below are primarily associated with AMD Software Adrenalin, automatic updates, telemetry, installation maintenance, and auxiliary software features.

        None of these tasks are normally required for day-to-day GPU operation, graphics rendering, gaming performance, hardware acceleration, or video playback acceleration.

        Some of them may provide software maintenance, update management, compatibility checks, AMD Link support, or other convenience features associated with AMD Software.

        For users seeking the lightest possible AMD installation and who do not rely on those features, I generally recommend disabling all of them.

        Scheduled Tasks Options

        AMDInstallLauncher

        Path: C:\Program Files\AMD\CIM\Bin64\InstallManagerApp.exe /InstallAUEP

        Launches AMD installation and maintenance processes used by AMD Software. This task is primarily responsible for software management, installation maintenance, and update-related operations. It is not required for gaming performance or graphics functionality.

        Recommendation: Disable it. It provides no benefit to gaming performance, image quality, or driver functionality and only supports AMD software maintenance activities.

        AMD COMPUTE

        Path: C:\Program Files\AMD\CIM\Bin64\InstallManagerApp.exe /AUTOUPDATEIN

        Associated with AMD software maintenance and update-related compute components. This task exists to support AMD software services and update mechanisms rather than graphics functionality.

        Recommendation: Disable it. Most users will never notice its absence, and removing it helps reduce unnecessary background activity.

        AMD Link Driver

        Path: C:\Program Files\AMD\CIM\Bin64\InstallManagerApp.exe -AMDLinkUpdate

        Supports AMD Link functionality. AMD Link allows remote monitoring, game streaming, and remote access features between devices. Most users never use AMD Link and have no need for its background services.

        Recommendation: Disable it unless you actively use AMD Link. For most users, it only adds unnecessary software overhead.

        AMD RELAUNCHER

        Path: C:\Program Files\AMD\CIM\Bin64\InstallManagerApp.exe /AUTOUPDATEIN

        Used to relaunch AMD software components after updates or configuration changes. It serves AMD Software maintenance purposes and is not required for normal GPU operation.

        Recommendation: Disable it. It has no impact on graphics performance and is only useful for AMD software management.

        AMDScoSupportTypeUpdate

        Path: C:\Program Files\AMD\CIM\Bin64\InstallManagerApp.exe /UpdateScoSupportType

        Updates internal AMD software compatibility and support information. This task exists primarily to support AMD Software features and update processes.

        Recommendation: Disable it. It provides no benefit to gaming, graphics performance, or driver stability.

        AMD Updater

        Path: C:\Program Files\AMD\CIM\Bin64\InstallManagerApp.exe /AUTOUPDATEIN

        Checks for and manages AMD driver and software updates. Users who manually install drivers generally do not need this functionality.

        Recommendation: Disable it if you prefer managing driver updates manually. It is not required for normal GPU operation.

        AMD UWP Launcher

        Path: C:\Program Files\AMD\CIM\Bin64\InstallManagerApp.exe /LaunchUWPApp

        Launches Microsoft Store (UWP) components associated with AMD Software. Only useful when using AMD's full software ecosystem.

        Recommendation: Disable it. Most users gain no practical benefit from this component.

        EnableWindowsDriverSearch

        Path: C:\Program Files\AMD\CIM\Bin64\InstallManagerApp.exe -EnableDriverSearch

        Allows Windows to automatically search for AMD driver updates. Some users prefer manual driver installation to avoid unwanted driver replacements.

        Recommendation: Disable it if you prefer managing driver updates manually. This task is associated with AMD's driver search and update mechanisms. Disabling it may reduce AMD-initiated driver search activity, although Windows Update may still install drivers depending on system configuration.

        AMDInstallUEP

        Path: C:\Program Files\AMD\InstallUEP\AMDInstallUEP.exe

        Part of AMD's User Experience Program. This task is associated with AMD's User Experience Program and may collect diagnostic information, software usage statistics, and telemetry data related to AMD Software and driver usage, depending on software configuration and participation settings.

        Recommendation: Disable it. It provides no direct benefit to gaming performance or graphics functionality and primarily exists for telemetry and diagnostic purposes.

        ModifyLinkUpdate

        Path: C:\Program Files\AMD\CIM\Bin64\InstallManagerApp.exe -UpdateCurrentUser

        Updates AMD Link configuration and user settings. This task is only relevant when using AMD Link features.

        Recommendation: Disable it unless you actively use AMD Link. Most users will never need this functionality.

        Recommended Scheduled Tasks Configuration

        For the lightest possible AMD installation, I generally recommend disabling all scheduled tasks.

        These tasks are primarily related to AMD Software maintenance, automatic updates, AMD Link functionality, and telemetry. None of them are required for graphics rendering, gaming performance, hardware acceleration, or normal GPU operation.

        Disabling them helps reduce background activity while maintaining full driver functionality.

        Radeon Software Slimmer - Display Driver Components Explanation

        Unlike scheduled tasks, the components listed below are actual driver components.

        Some are essential for compatibility and graphics functionality, while others are optional depending on how the system is used.

        For a lightweight gaming-focused installation, some components can be safely removed while others should always be kept.

        Display Driver Components

        High Definition Audio Bus

        Dir: \Packages\Drivers\Display\WT6A_INF\amdafd | INF: amdafd.inf

        Provides HDMI and DisplayPort audio support. This component allows audio to be transmitted directly through the graphics card to monitors, televisions, AV receivers, soundbars, and other audio devices connected through HDMI or DisplayPort.

        Recommendation: Keep it if you use HDMI or DisplayPort audio in any form. If all audio is handled exclusively by motherboard audio, USB audio devices, or a dedicated sound card, it can usually be removed. If your monitor has built-in speakers, a headphone jack, or any audio functionality delivered through HDMI or DisplayPort, this component should remain installed.

        AMD Dynamic Audio Noise Suppression

        Dir: \Packages\Drivers\Display\WT6A_INF\amdfdans | INF: AMDFDANS.inf

        Provides AMD's AI-powered microphone noise suppression technology. This feature helps reduce unwanted background noise during voice communication in applications such as Discord, Teams, Zoom, and in-game voice chat.

        Recommendation: Remove it unless you specifically use AMD Noise Suppression. Users who do not rely on this feature for voice communication will generally not notice its absence.

        AMD Crash Defender

        Dir: \Packages\Drivers\Display\WT6A_INF\amdfendr | INF: amdfendr.inf

        Provides crash recovery and protection mechanisms for AMD graphics drivers. It can help Windows recover from certain GPU driver crashes without requiring a full system reboot.

        Recommendation: Keep it. Although not strictly required for graphics functionality, it can improve driver recovery behavior and overall system stability in the event of a GPU-related crash.

        AMD OpenCL User Mode Driver

        Dir: \Packages\Drivers\Display\WT6A_INF\amdocl | INF: amdocl.inf

        Provides OpenCL support for GPU-accelerated computing workloads. OpenCL is used by various applications, including rendering software, media encoders, video editing suites, scientific computing tools, and certain AI or compute workloads.

        Recommendation: If your system is used exclusively for gaming, this component can usually be removed without affecting game performance. However, some productivity, media encoding, rendering, AI, and compute applications may require OpenCL functionality. Users who rely on such software should keep it installed.

        OpenGL Driver

        Dir: \Packages\Drivers\Display\WT6A_INF\amdogl | INF: amdogl.inf

        Provides OpenGL graphics API support. While many modern games use DirectX or Vulkan, OpenGL remains necessary for numerous games, emulators, CAD applications, engineering software, and professional workloads.

        Recommendation: Keep it. The compatibility benefits significantly outweigh the negligible space savings gained by removing it.

        AMD PCI Bridge Device Extension

        Dir: \Packages\Drivers\Display\WT6A_INF\amdpcibridge | INF: amdpcibridgeextension.inf

        Provides low-level PCI Express communication and integration between the graphics card and the operating system. This is considered a core driver component required for proper hardware communication and device operation.

        Recommendation: Keep it. Removing this component is not recommended and may result in compatibility or functionality issues.

        AMD Vulkan Driver

        Dir: \Packages\Drivers\Display\WT6A_INF\amdvlk | INF: amdvlk.inf

        Provides Vulkan API support. Many modern games and applications rely on Vulkan directly or indirectly, making it one of the most important graphics components included in the driver package.

        Recommendation: Keep it. Removing this component may cause compatibility problems and prevent certain games or applications from functioning correctly.

        AMD Windows Support Components

        Dir: \Packages\Drivers\Display\WT6A_INF\amdwin | INF: amdwin-u0201164.inf

        Provides Windows integration components used by the AMD driver stack. These components help ensure proper communication and integration between the AMD graphics driver and the Windows operating system.

        Recommendation: Keep it. It is considered a core part of the AMD driver package and should remain installed.

        AMD Controller Emulation

        Dir: \Packages\Drivers\Display\WT6A_INF\amdxe | INF: amdxe.inf

        AMD does not publicly document this component in detail. It appears to provide internal compatibility and support functionality used by certain AMD driver features. Because its exact role is not fully documented, removing it may introduce compatibility issues in some driver configurations.

        Recommendation: Keep it. The space savings gained by removing it are negligible, while keeping it helps maximize compatibility and minimize the risk of unexpected driver behavior.

        Recommended Minimal Driver Configuration

        For a clean, lightweight, and compatibility-focused AMD driver installation, the following components are generally recommended:

        Required:

        • AMD PCI Bridge Device Extension
        • AMD Vulkan Driver
        • AMD Windows Support Components
        • AMD Controller Emulation
        • OpenGL Driver
        • AMD Crash Defender

        Optional:

        • High Definition Audio Bus (only if HDMI or DisplayPort audio is not used)
        • AMD OpenCL User Mode Driver (only if OpenCL-dependent applications are not used)
        • AMD Dynamic Audio Noise Suppression (only if the feature is not used)

        This configuration provides full graphics functionality, broad game compatibility, and excellent stability while minimizing unnecessary optional components.

        Although removing optional components may slightly reduce installation size and component count, it is not expected to produce measurable improvements to gaming performance, FPS, input latency, GPU responsiveness, or overall graphics performance.

        NVCleanstall Tweaks & Options

        Below you will find a detailed explanation of each tweak and option available in NVCleanstall's installation customization screen, along with my personal recommendations for each one.

        Installation Options

        Disable Installer Telemetry & Advertising

        Disables telemetry and advertising included in the NVIDIA installer. This reduces the amount of data collected during installation and prevents unnecessary components from being installed.

        Recommendation: Enable it. There are no downsides.

        Unattended Express Installation

        Performs an automatic installation without requiring any additional user confirmation. It is mainly intended for users who need to install drivers on multiple systems or want to fully automate the process.

        Recommendation: Leave it disabled. For a customized installation, it's better to review each step manually.

        Perform a Clean Installation

        Removes previous NVIDIA settings and installs the drivers as if it were the first installation on the system. This can help resolve issues caused by corrupted configurations or leftover settings.

        Recommendation: Always enable it, especially when updating drivers or reinstalling Windows.

        Add Hardware Support

        Allows support to be added for hardware that is not officially recognized by NVIDIA drivers.

        Recommendation: Leave it disabled. Only enable it if you know exactly why you need it.

        Enable DLSS Indicator

        Displays an on-screen indicator showing when DLSS is active and which version is being used by the game.

        Recommendation: Enable it only if you want to verify that DLSS is working. It is not necessary for normal use.

        Disable Multiplane Overlay (MPO)

        Disables Windows' MPO feature, which can cause flickering, black screens, browser issues, stuttering, or other unusual behavior in games on some systems.

        Recommendation: Enable it. Many users have resolved stability issues with this option.

        Disable Ansel

        Disables NVIDIA Ansel, a feature that allows advanced screenshot capture in supported games.

        Recommendation: If you do not use NVIDIA Ansel, enable it. Most users never use this feature.

        Show Expert Tweaks

        Displays NVCleanstall's advanced settings.

        Recommendation: Enable it to access all available optimizations.

        Expert Tweaks

        Disable Driver Telemetry

        Disables telemetry built directly into the NVIDIA drivers, reducing data collection and some background activity.

        Recommendation: Enable it. This is one of the most recommended options for a clean installation.

        Disable NVIDIA Container

        Disables NVIDIA Container, a service used by several NVIDIA features, including the NVIDIA Control Panel.

        Recommendation: Do not enable it. You may lose access to the NVIDIA Control Panel and other important functionality.

        Disable NVIDIA HD Audio Device Sleep Timer

        Prevents the NVIDIA audio device connected through HDMI or DisplayPort from repeatedly entering power-saving mode.

        Recommendation: Enable it. It can help prevent audio delays and device detection issues.

        Enable Message Signaled Interrupts (MSI Mode)

        Allows the graphics card to use the modern MSI interrupt system, reducing CPU overhead and slightly improving system responsiveness.

        Recommendation: Enable it. It is generally considered one of the most useful optimizations.

        Interrupt Policy

        Determines how Windows handles GPU interrupts.

        Recommendation: Leave it set to the default value unless you know exactly what you are doing.

        Interrupt Priority

        Allows you to assign a priority level to GPU interrupts.

        Recommendation: Set it to High to give the GPU higher interrupt priority.

        Disable HDCP

        Disables HDCP, the digital content protection system used by services such as Netflix, Disney+, Prime Video, and protected Blu-ray content.

        Recommendation: Enable it if you do not watch protected 4K content. If you use streaming services or protected media, leave it disabled.

        Apply NVENC Video Encoding Session Limit Patch

        Removes NVIDIA's limit on the number of simultaneous NVENC video encoding sessions.

        Recommendation: If you only use your PC for gaming, leave it disabled. Enable it only if you use professional streaming, encoding, or multi-recording software.

        Start External Application

        Allows a program to be launched automatically after the installation is completed.

        Recommendation: Leave it disabled. It is not necessary for normal use.

        Signature & Anti-Cheat Compatibility

        Rebuild Digital Signature

        Rebuilds the driver's digital signature when certain modifications require a custom driver package to be generated.

        Recommendation: If NVCleanstall enables it automatically, leave it enabled.

        Use Method Compatible with Easy Anti-Cheat

        Uses a signing method that is compatible with Easy Anti-Cheat and other anti-cheat systems.

        Recommendation: Always enable it to avoid potential issues in online games.

        Automatically Accept the "Driver Unsigned" Warning

        Automatically accepts Windows warnings related to modified or custom drivers.

        Recommendation: Enable it to make the installation process simpler and more automated.
